headline: Deep learning models advance gene annotation, protein function and metagenome binning
label: Deep Learning Genomics Tools
summary: Recent preprints and a publication extend deep learning tools to multi-clade gene prediction, structure-based function annotation and metagenomic binning.
synthesis: The common thread is deep learning applied to genomic and protein sequence-derived data for annotation and classification, with each item positioned against established methods. Tiberius extends its deep-learning ab initio gene predictor beyond mammals, with lineage-specific models across six eukaryotic clades benchmarked on 33 species. OrionGeno is a phylogeny-aware model for ab initio eukaryotic genome annotation that outperforms existing methods. Metagenomic-deepFRI adds structural templates to protein function annotation at sequence-alignment-like speeds, improving GO-based function annotation. TaxVAMB, a semisupervised bimodal variational autoencoder, bins metagenomic contigs using coabundance, tetranucleotide frequencies and taxonomic labels. What is new is the tooling itself and its benchmarks, with contributions framed as method performance rather than biological findings.
